Conductor short-circuit withstand not checked: give fault_clearing_s.
Not checked: shield short-circuit withstand; mutual heating between stacked tiers.
Shields bonded both ends: max circulating current 60 A, shield loss 1.88 kW (12.5 % of conductor loss). Single-point or cross bonding removes most of this.
Voltage drop by phase, exact / approximate I(R cos phi + X sin phi) form, each against its own sending-end phase voltage: A 0.06 / 0.06 %, B 0.07 / 0.07 %, C 0.05 / 0.05 %.

Enclosure (6063-T6, sides only): induced current up to 364 A per wall, loss 0.54 kW (3.6 % of conductor loss). Longitudinal circulating current only; transverse eddy and hysteresis (none in Al) not included.
Magnetic field (RMS resultant) side 0.3 m: 30.69 uT, top 0.3 m: 28.92 uT, side 1 m: 3.52 uT, top 1 m: 7.13 uT. Reference levels at 60 Hz: ICNIRP 1998 public 83.3 uT, occupational 416.7 uT.

sheath.recommendation: Single-point bonding: 5.0 V at the open end of a 61 m bonded section at normal load (101 V during a 40 kA balanced through-fault), no circulating loss. Both-ends bonding: 60 A circulating, 1.88 kW shield loss, worst lambda1 0.180, lowest cable ampacity 892 -> 848 A, worst loading 76.6 -> 79.5 %. Set your utility / owner standing-voltage limit to get a pass/fail and a recommendation. Cross-bonding is not modelled.
notes: No verified public limit is loaded: a secondary source attributes ~25 V at normal load to IEEE 575 practice (LOW confidence, clause not found), so it is not used as a default. Set the utility / owner limit (shield_voltage_limit_v) to get a pass/fail.

Through-fault voltage assumes a balanced three-phase fault shared like load current; a single-line-to-ground fault (earth / shield return) can give much higher shield voltages and is not modelled. Compare the fault value with the jacket and sheath voltage limiter (SVL) ratings.
Cross-bonding (three equal minor sections with transpositions) is not modelled.
